products.title: Los Angeles Typographic Poster
products.body_html:
This map accurately depicts the major streets and highways, parks, coastlines, and physical features of Los Angeles using nothing but type. Every single piece of type was manually placed, a process that took hundreds of hours to complete.

From the Hollywood sign and downtown Los Angeles, to the tip of Rancho Palos Verdes and Long Beach, a map of Los Angeles is stitched together from thousands of manually-placed words and letters. The Pacific Ocean, home of some of the best surfing in the world, gets prime of place with its very own Wingdings surfer dude. The Beach City areas of Santa Monica, Manhattan Beach, and Redondo Beach also make an appearance. LA's famous highways are shown in bold purple lettering.

The map is based on place names and geography as they appear in Open Street Map.

products.title: San Francisco Typographic Framed Poster
products.body_html:
This map accurately depicts the streets and highways, parks, neighborhoods, coastlines, and physical features of San Francisco using nothing but type. Every single piece of type was manually placed, a process that took hundreds of hours to complete.

The map contains the entire city of San Francisco and is one of our densest maps (in terms of letters per inch) showing the largest highways at 12 pt and the smallest surface streets at 6 pt condensed. The Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay are also depicted using a modern take on an old fashioned ‘water line’ mapping technique. Although not mapped directly, the famous hilly topography of the city is clearly seen in the twists and curves of many of the streets.

The map is based on place names and geography as they appear in Open Street Map.

products.title: London Typographic Framed Poster

products.title: Boston Typographic Framed Poster
products.body_html:
This is the 2nd edition of our popular Boston map, first introduced back in 2010. Like that earlier map, this new edition accurately depicts the streets and highways, parks, neighborhoods, coastlines, and physical features of the city using nothing but type. Every single piece of type was manually placed, a process that took hundreds of hours to complete.

Most notably, the 2nd edition covers a much larger area than before, extending from Medford and Malden in the north all the way down to Dedham, Milton, and the Blue Hills Reservation in the south. Watertown marks its western extent, with the airport and harbor forming the eastern boundary of the map. This means that we now include over half a million more people on the map than we had previously! In the center of the map is the entire city of Boston proper, along with Cambridge, Somerville, and other towns across the Charles River.

To make the 2nd edition, we started from scratch with the latest geographic data and place names from Open Street Map. In addition, we gave the map a fresh new design. New water styling is reminiscent of our Washington, DC map, displayed as reversed out white text on a dark blue background. Parks and institutions follow suit with their respective background colors. The result is a bolder look with higher contrast that gives the map more definition and makes some features, like small parks, narrow rivers, and jetties, easier to see.
